NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks vertical displacement and surface cracking as separate indicators.
My observable is the coupling coefficient between vertical displacement rate and local surface strain energy density, which captures the hidden interaction between bulk creep and surface degradation.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
The observable is calculated from existing strain gauges and displacement sensors using standard finite element analysis routines already in the bridge monitoring system.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks vertical displacement and surface cracking as separate indicators. My observable is the coupling coefficient between vertical displacement rate and local surface strain energy density, which captures the hidden interaction between bulk creep and surface degradation. This coupling coefficient increases as micro-damage accumulates in the elastomer, providing early warning before either displacement or cracking alone exceeds thresholds.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing physical relation is: K = (dδ/dt) / (U/ρ), where K is the coupling coefficient, dδ/dt is the vertical displacement rate, U is the strain energy density, and ρ is the material density. For a healthy elastomer, K should be approximately 0.1-0.2 MPa·s/m. As creep and surface damage progress, K increases to 0.5-1.0 MPa·s/m before failure thresholds are reached.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
Components: Existing strain gauge array on bearing surface, existing displacement transducers, existing data acquisition system
Materials: None new required
Instruments: Standard finite element analysis software (already in use)
Procedure: Calculate strain energy density from strain gauge data, measure vertical displacement rate, compute coupling coefficient K weekly
Development needed: Custom script to extract and process the required data streams (standard engineering work)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
Installability: Same as standard practice - no additional hardware
Operability: Same data collection frequency as standard practice
Maintenance: No additional maintenance requirements
Cost class: Same as standard practice - only software development cost (one-time)
The approach maintains the same deployment burden while providing a more sensitive early warning indicator.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Install test bearings in accelerated aging chamber with cyclic loading and ozone exposure. Monitor standard displacement and crack metrics alongside coupling coefficient K.
Instruments: Existing bridge monitoring sensors, environmental chamber, crack detection microscope
Pass threshold: K remains below 0.3 MPa·s/m after 75-year equivalent aging
Fail threshold: K exceeds 0.5 MPa·s/m before displacement or crack thresholds
Duration: 6 months of accelerated aging (equivalent to 75 years)
Kill criterion: Any bearing showing K > 0.5 MPa·s/m before test completion falsifies the approach
